title: GNA Energy
headline: India's power market, made readable.
card: An over-the-counter electricity-trading platform, its analytics and the company website. Dense, high-stakes screens for traders, generators and admins.
summary: Two and a half years as UI/UX designer at GNA Energy, which runs a CERC-regulated over-the-counter platform where companies buy and sell electricity. I designed the trading platform, its analytics dashboards, the Vidyut AI assistant, a reusable UI kit and the company website.
meta: Trading platform, analytics, AI assistant, website, UI kit

r: Many markets, many roles, one screen at a time.

Electricity is traded in very different ways: bilateral deals, reverse and forward auctions, competitive bidding, RFQs, banking, battery storage and renewable certificates. Each comes with its own quantities, rates, time slots and deadlines.
The same platform also serves consumers, generators, traders, company admins and a super admin.
The challenge was to make a dense, high-stakes product feel calm without hiding anything a trader needs.

items: Bilateral, auctions, RFQ, banking, BESS, REC and VPPA, each with its own rules.
Quantity, energy rate, dates, time blocks and expiry on every listing.
Consumers, generators, traders and admins need different views of the same deals.

r: A single navigation for every product.
Banking, RFP/RFQ, Buy/Sell, BESS, REC and VPPA live in one sidebar, so switching markets never means learning a new layout.
Quantity, energy rate, type, region, dates and times sit in the same grid on every card, with status chips for On hold, Active and Accepted.
Edit, ledger, chat, download and duplicate sit on each listing, and the live market sits right beside your own listings.
Shared buttons, chips, tables and cards across every flow. It cut design-to-dev time by 25%.

body.alt: Buy/Sell dashboard: your listings on the left, the live market on the right.

r: Buy/Sell dashboard: your listings on the left, the live market on the right.
Analytics that answer, not just display.
I designed analytics dashboards for power-market data used by traders and analysts. Clearer charts, filters and comparisons

: an assistant that lets traders ask about prices and forecasts in plain language instead of digging through several dashboards. I designed the conversation flow, answer cards and chart responses, and tested them with traders. Five screens became one question.

body.alt: GNAi insights platform: market trends across exchanges, by product and by time.

r: GNAi insights platform: market trends across exchanges, by product and by time.
A website that explains the platform in one screen.
I redesigned gna.energy with a clearer structure, a modern visual language and responsive layouts. The hero says what GNA is, who regulates it and where to start. Enquiries went up by 20%.

body.alt: gna.energy home: the platform, the regulator and the first step, above the fold.

r: gna.energy home: the platform, the regulator and the first step, above the fold.
A trading platform, analytics suite and website that share one design language, with measurable gains in speed and enquiries.

title: The Invisible Dead Zones
headline: Designing Wi‑Fi that follows a family through their home.
card: Streams dropped in one bedroom every night. Nobody said the network was broken. A one-day sprint that treats a home network like a product.
summary: A one-day design-thinking sprint on an everyday problem: unreliable Wi-Fi across a multi-floor home. The goal was a better network without buying a faster plan.

r: The complaints were small. The pattern wasn't.
Streams dropped in bedroom two, mostly at night. The third floor, meant for work and entertainment, couldn't hold a video call. The hall mostly worked.
a problem with the space, not the internet plan.
Problems followed location, not time of day.

items: Move with people. Hall by day, bedrooms by night.
Can never drop. Steady streaming, always-on voice.
Smart devices. Some only join 2.4 GHz networks.
Barely usable. Fit for texts, not for calls.

r: I walked both floors and the staircase with a pencil, noting the router, the rooms and how the signal felt in each. The sketch was redrawn to scale at 30′ × 40′ and became the base for a 3D model of the house.
The brief changed once the evidence came in.
“We need the connection we already have to reach
That reframe ruled out the most obvious idea, a faster plan, before a rupee was spent.
Eight ideas. A tie at the top. Evidence broke it.
From free fixes to a second internet line, each option was scored 1–5 on coverage, one seamless network, ease, reliability, room to grow and cost.
Both mesh options scored 24. Starting with two avoids paying for a node before the data shows it's needed.
Keep the ISP router, run the mesh in access-point mode.
Removes the second router layer and the duplicate network that devices kept clinging to.
Retire the old Wi-Fi only after verifying.
Turning off duplicate Wi-Fi scores low on its own but is essential to one clean network.
Place the satellite by data, not guesswork.
Its spot follows backhaul quality measured on the third floor.

body.alt: The full case study is built as an interactive visual story around a 3D model of the house.

r: The full case study is built as an interactive visual story around a 3D model of the house.
The sprint ends at a decision: a two-unit mesh, with a before-and-after scoreboard ready for six spots in the house.
“It buffers in R2” was the real insight. Where and when mattered more than any spec sheet.
The same house has a day map and a night map. Designing for one would miss half the family.
A speed test is a snapshot. Being clear about what data proves kept me from over-claiming.
Mode, placement and retiring the old network are the real design work.
Implement. Measure. Update this story, even if the data says I was wrong.
Next steps: baseline speed tests in six spots, switch modes, place the satellite, reconnect devices, then re-measure in the same spots with the same method.

title: Lyftrr
headline: Show the mechanism. Skip the claims.
card: Mentorship in India runs on luck. A ten-chapter launch page for a platform that matches people to someone one rung above them.
summary: Lyftrr matches people climbing in their careers with someone a rung or two above them, for six-week, scoped “lifts”. It is pre-launch, so the page had to earn trust without a product to demo.

r: No product to demo, no logos, no case studies.

A conventional landing page in that position has to make claims, and claims from an unlaunched company read as noise. Meanwhile the problem Lyftrr solves is real: good guidance depends on who you happen to know.

items: Well-meaning, but from outside the field.
A general answer to a specific situation.
Serious guidance costs too much to try twice.

r: The product is about climbing. So the page is a climb.

: the reading, the gap, the match, the six weeks, the record. One night sky runs behind all ten chapters; scrolling is the argument. By the signup, the visitor has travelled the distance the product promises.

body.alt: Two ways to move: one staircase, read from the Riser's and the Lifter's side.

r: Two ways to move: one staircase, read from the Riser's and the Lifter's side.
Every choice traces back to three goals.
Say what Lyftrr does within ten seconds. Read as funded and serious. End every path in a waitlist signup tagged Riser or Lifter.
Risers are the volume audience, so theirs is filled. Lifters are scarce and high-value, so theirs is outlined: present, not competing.
A Riser/Lifter switch and a live engine panel cycling Signal → Gap → Match → Lift → Proof, so visitors operate the product before they're asked for anything.
A pinned sequence from Day 0 to Week 6 answers “this will fizzle out” structurally, with a start date, an end date and a filed record.
Ad-hoc colours consolidated into one system. The brand gradient appears only where something is live or worth acting on.

body.alt: The long view: one lift is a favour, twelve is a trajectory.

r: The long view: one lift is a favour, twelve is a trajectory.
Designed for the thumb, not stacked.

Every chapter was taken through 360, 390 and 430 px. Touch targets are at least 44 px, small instrument labels are raised to a legible floor, and pinned sequences become swipeable strips that tell the same beat. No horizontal overflow at any width.

body.alt: The problem, drawn one fault at a time.

r: The problem, drawn one fault at a time.

body.alt: The platform, as floors you climb instead of a feature grid.

r: The platform, as floors you climb instead of a feature grid.

body.alt: The ladder: three rungs of indicative pricing, opening with Batch 01.

r: The ladder: three rungs of indicative pricing, opening with Batch 01.
Built and responsive across ten chapters, now in review with the founding team.
Real photography of Risers and Lifters, live waitlist numbers instead of indicative ones, and the first three completed lifts written up as proof.

title: FreeKaaMaal
headline: Helping deal-hunters find the right deal, faster.
card: Shoppers arrived knowing what they wanted and still had to dig. A calmer deal card, intent-led navigation and fewer steps to save.
summary: A revamp of one of India's deals and cashback platforms: cleaner layouts, navigation built around intent, and quicker paths from browsing to saving.

r: One job to do well, buried under noise.
Users came with a clear goal: a deal for a store or a product. Cluttered pages, complex navigation and slow loads pushed bounce rates up.

items: Dense pages hid the deals that mattered.
Too many steps to reach a store or category.
Page weight directly affected bounce rate.

r: Shoppers searched by store and category, not by browsing.

Inconsistent deal formats made comparison slow, and the coupon and cashback steps confused first-time users. With thousands of offers changing daily, a strong system mattered more than any single page.

body.alt: App home and store search: offers, deal stories and popular brands up front.

r: App home and store search: offers, deal stories and popular brands up front.
Three changes that did the most.
Navigation rebuilt around categories, stores and search, so relevant deals surface in a few taps.
A consistent card system on calmer pages that puts the saving first.
Reveal code, copy, go: a simplified coupon and cashback flow on lighter pages.

body.alt: Wallet and cashback history: what you've earned, at a glance.

r: Wallet and cashback history: what you've earned, at a glance.

body.alt: Deal stories, flash sales and search results.

r: Deal stories, flash sales and search results.
Clearer navigation lifted engagement and conversion, with one deal-card system keeping thousands of offers easy to scan.

title: Woost
headline: Bringing transparency to influencer marketing, in a 14-day sprint.
card: Brands couldn't see ROI and creators couldn't find the right brands. A two-sided app designed end to end in two weeks.
summary: A two-sided marketplace that matches brands with the right creators, tracks deliverables automatically and shows campaign performance in real time.
chips: Mobile app · UI kit · Live on Google Play
meta: Mobile app, live on Google Play
Research, flows, app UI, UI kit

r: A marketplace only works when both sides trust it.
Influencer marketing ran on guesswork. Briefs, approvals and deliverables lived in DMs and spreadsheets, and existing platforms offered no live insight.

items: Brands couldn't see reliable reach or ROI.
Briefs and approvals scattered across DMs.
The right creator was hard to find, and vice versa.

r: Focus the sprint on the core loop.
Brief, match, invite, track. I built the UI kit first, so fourteen days produced a complete, consistent product instead of disconnected screens.

body.alt: The creator journey: explore campaigns, read the brief, track status, get paid.

r: The creator journey: explore campaigns, read the brief, track status, get paid.
Creators valued clear terms, deliverables and payout before applying.
Milestones tracked automatically, from application approved to payout released.
A wallet with total earnings, available balance and every payout.

body.alt: Campaign brief and application status.
Wallet with earnings and payouts.

r: From blank canvas to dev-ready in 14 days, giving brands control over campaigns and creators a transparent way to collaborate.

title: Rahul Nandan Sir
headline: Rebuilding a chemistry educator's website to turn visitors into students.
card: Website redesign for an IIT JEE & NEET educator
summary: A leading chemistry educator's website that didn't match his reputation. I restructured the content, simplified navigation and built a bold visual system that works on every screen.
meta: Audit, IA, UI, prototype, UI kit

r: Visitors arrived with intent but left quickly: no clear hierarchy, hidden navigation, branding that shifted page to page, and layouts that broke on mobile, where most traffic came from.
Pages rebuilt around what visitors came for, with one clear action: book a demo.
A dark canvas with warm orange and yellow accents, applied through a reusable UI kit.
Responsive layouts designed for the phone first.

body.alt: Homepage and courses.
About page: story, vision and work history.

r: About page: story, vision and work history.
A credible, on-brand home that's clearer to navigate and easy to extend with the UI kit.

title: Chemistry Shiksha
headline: Turning a chemistry teacher's content into an exam-prep platform.
card: Exam-prep platform for IIT-JEE & NEET students
summary: Chemistry Shiksha is Rahul Nandan Sir's learning platform for IIT-JEE, NEET, Olympiad and board exams. I designed it around how students actually prepare: by exam, by class and by topic.

r: Students don't browse. They prepare for one exam.
A JEE aspirant and a Class 11 student want very different things from the same content. So the site has three entry points, exam-wise, class-wise and topic-wise, each with its own home page.
Line-by-line NCERT questions, exemplar questions and diagram-based questions are the first thing students see.
Previous-year questions for 15 exams, from JEE Main and NEET to BITSAT, KVPY and AIIMS.
Test packages sorted by exam, class or topic, with price, validity and number of tests on every card.

body.alt: Chapter-wise PYQ bank across 15 entrance exams.

r: Chapter-wise PYQ bank across 15 entrance exams.

body.alt: Test packages, filtered by exam, topic or class.

r: Test packages, filtered by exam, topic or class.
One platform with three ways in, built so a student reaches a practice question in one or two taps.

title: Jai Singh & Company
headline: One brand for a company that builds highways, railways and toll systems.
card: Corporate website for an infrastructure group
summary: A website for Jai Singh and Company (JSC), a business group working in mining, national highway tolling, railways, infrastructure, consultancy and software. The brief: present a broad, technical business as one confident brand.

r: JSC works across very different sectors. A visitor from a highway authority and one looking for manpower services both had to understand the company in a few seconds.
Products, years of experience and completed projects sit right next to who JSC is.
Railways, manpower and national highways shown through real site photography.
Deep navy, light trails and a map texture that match an infrastructure business.

body.alt: Who we are, with the numbers alongside.

r: Who we are, with the numbers alongside.

body.alt: Services carousel with on-site photography.

r: A clear, credible front door for a multi-sector infrastructure group.

title: SIBSTC
headline: Making mandatory bank training something staff actually finish.
card: Website and learning platform for a bank staff training college
summary: A redesign of the Southern India Banks' Staff Training College website and learning platform, turning scattered modules into a clear, mobile-first learning journey.

r: Staff trained in short bursts, on their phones.
Bank staff completed training between shifts, but navigation was confusing, modules had no clear order, progress was hard to track and accessibility was limited.

items: Hard to find and resume assigned modules.

r: Design for short sessions and small screens.
Modular courses with visible progress, so staff always know what's next.
Simplified navigation that keeps learners moving.
Mobile-first, accessible screens that fit a banker's day.

body.alt: Programmes, filterable by category.
Infrastructure, browsable by facility.
Mobile-first: about and infrastructure on a phone.

r: Mobile-first: about and infrastructure on a phone.
Staff reported a smoother experience, with better retention and wider adoption of training programmes.
